THREE DIFFERENCES FROM THE BASE, all governed away by base-over-ALT, so the app drawing none of them MATCHES: the divider itself; the 8/rule/8 split of the seam, against the base's flat 12 (which the band's `pt-3` already pays); and a leading mark on the selected sort, which here is `Frame 631` 8575:81738 74 wide wrapping a 16 icons/action at x=0 and a 54 label at x=20, where the base draws Trending as a bare 57-wide CTA/button. (1) Frame 630 1318x36: the 420 title group, the nav at (459.5,7) 399x22 - the SAME 399 run the 375 board overflows its column with, here fitting - and a 420 right group at x=898 with a 16 glyph at x=356 and a 36 CTA at x=384. (2) the promo band at y=68, 1318x141: TWO 659 cards side by side, the right one's Title at (32,32) 475x77, against 768's two 354s at 110 and 375's single EMPTY 150. THE DEPOSIT CARD IS TWO COLUMNS HERE where both narrow boards stack: data at (16,16) 938x24 ("Deposit to pool" 116x24, and the wallet link is the FULL sentence "Open wallet to see activity" 155x18 at x=725 where 375 truncates it to "Open wallet" 61x14), a rule at 56, then Frame 309 at (16,72) 938x498 = a 461 plan column at x=0 and a 461 form column at x=477, 16 apart. THE PLAN COLUMN IS THE FINDING: "Select plan" 67x18, 10, then a 461x444 grid of THREE 140-tall rows 12 apart, each holding two 224.5 cards 12 apart, each card a 192.5x108 middle at (16,16) - and all five tiers are drawn at once, with only Ninety's 32x32 radio visible: Flex 6.0% (Lock None, Exit Free, a two-row description), Thirty 11.0% (Bonus 1%, Lock 30 days, Exit 4% pro-rata), Ninety 16.0% (Bonus 6%, Lock 90 days, Exit 10% pro-rata), One-eighty 20.0% (Bonus 10%, Lock 180 days, Exit 15% pro-rata), One-year 25.0% (Bonus 15%, Lock 365 days, Exit 20% pro-rata). ★ THAT TABLE IS DESIGN COPY, NOT A SOURCE - but it maps one-to-one onto a real one, and naming it is what this pass was for. SKAITradingVault exposes tierConfigs(tier) returning [lockDuration, apyBps, penaltyBps] against the LockTier enum 0 Flex, 1 ThirtyDay, 2 NinetyDay, 3 OneEightyDay, 4 ThreeSixtyFiveDay, read live by src/hooks/vault/useTradingVaultData.ts with per-tier revert tolerance and isLive / partial / chainUnavailable already on the shape. BONUS DOES NOT, on any tier: tierConfigs returns three values and none of them is a bonus, so 1% / 6% / 10% / 15% stand on nothing. NEITHER DOES THE RAIL. The house pool has no Solana rail and a UI lane must not open one. SO THE CARD STAYS UNBUILT AND THIS ROW STAYS OPEN, exactly as ruled, and nothing was invented. The board: 76.268x108 tile, radius 6.254, ground bg-[#001615], fill 11703.png at h-[117.7%] left-0 top-[-3%] w-full, gradient from-[rgba(18,63,60,0)] at 41.823% to-[#123f3c] at 78.7% over a backdrop-blur-[1.067px], caption 10296:5159 51.506 wide at (12.1,83) on a 3.122 gap running Manrope ExtraBold 9.365/9.365 -0.3746 uppercase Slide over Mulish 4.292/5.463 -0.1717 Skai Originals at 64% opacity, inset shadow 0/0.427/10.666 rgba(8,8,8,0.14), drop 0/0.391/1.564 rgba(0,0,0,0.75). THE CROP IS THE WHOLE ROW AND IT IS NOW SHIPPED. w-full with h-[117.7%] IS an exact cover fit on this cut and not a zoom, which is the check that makes the rest of the arithmetic safe: slide.webp on disk is 1080x1800, aspect exactly 0.600000, and a 0.6 raster scaled to the width of a 274:388 box (0.7061856, which is the cover cards own 76.268:108) stands (1/0.6)/(1/0.7061856) = 117.70% of that box tall - the frame number to four figures. So the only free parameter is the vertical anchor, and the frames top-[-3%] hides 3/117.7 = 2.549% of the raster above the card and shows 2.549%..87.51%. The map ships object-position, so the band start is Y x the cut overflow, and both overflows were recomputed here from the raster and the classes in PlayGameCard.tsx: rail RAIL_ASPECT aspect-[274/388] at :78 overflows 1 - 0.6/(274/388) = 15.0365%, featured aspect-[317/409] at :83 overflows 22.5867%. The exact solutions are therefore 2.549/0.150365 = 16.95% on the rail cut and 2.549/0.225867 = 11.29% on the featured one, two different numbers for one shipped value, so the compromise is CHECKED rather than assumed: the shipped 50% 14% lands the band at 2.105% on the rail and 3.162% on the featured, 0.44pp and 0.61pp off the frames 2.549%, both inside the 1.5pp this map holds itself to - which is the same test that REJECTED a midpoint on the Desktop card, where it fell 1.65pp out. The Desktop value alone did not hold here: 50% 36% puts the rail band at 5.413%, 2.86pp off this board, and this is the first pair on the cover page whose Mobile card is not its Desktop scaled down. Landed in a3c7050a (already on origin/main when this lane opened, so the code was committed and the row was the only thing missing) as artPositionMobile on the slide entry at playGameArt.ts:1040, typed at :781 and threaded to the FIVE hub call sites that draw a tile - Play.tsx:2149 (into PlayGameRail, read at PlayGameRail.tsx:158) and Play.tsx:3345, TrendingGames.tsx:318, ContinuePlaying.tsx:346, PlayCollectionView.tsx:676 - so the prop is mounted and not an orphan, which is checked here by grep rather than by the component test alone. PlayGameCard.tsx:384 artStyle sends both values out as custom properties because an inline style cannot carry a breakpoint, and :601 picks between them with [object-position:var(--art-pos-sm)] lg:[object-position:var(--art-pos)]; a game with no Mobile value keeps the plain objectPosition it always had, so no other tile moves. The lg switch is VERIFIED not assumed: TILE_RADIUS.rail at PlayGameCard.tsx:112 is rounded-[12px] lg:rounded-[16px], so the position changes shell where the tile does, and 768 - which has no slide cover board of its own - inherits this 375 reading rather than the Desktop one. MEASURED AND RECORDED, NOT A DEFECT: the img also carries scale-[1.02] at rest, which narrows the visible band to 83.29% of the raster and moves the start to 2.94%, 0.39pp the other side of the frame; it is a whole-map systematic every tile has carried since before this prop existed and the map solves against the unscaled geometry by convention, so it is stated here rather than corrected under one game. Second witness file modules/skai-gaming/src/components/play/ui/PlayGameCard.artPositionMobile.test.tsx, which the carried note called eight assertions and which is in fact ELEVEN tests, all green this pass - the note was wrong about its own size, which is why the figure here is the run output.

M6r9FEn042UWTQD1zvy6GM:10407-13075.notes: RE-EXAMINED AT HEAD THIS PASS RATHER THAN CARRIED, because three waves have recorded this as unbuildable and a reason not to act is the note least often re-read. The composition is not in doubt and is unchanged: Overlay at .34 with no blur; a 112x288 streak centred with its bottom 140 below the panel (10407:14054); the astronaut 176x210 upright centred at (50%+0.5, 50%+92); the logo 128x61 at (50%+0.5, 50%-161.5); no grid, no bar, no text. WHAT IS NEW: the engine DOES have a state whose shape matches, and it was missed because it is a consequence of two files rather than a named scene. BootScene.relayout() (BootScene.ts) is this.scene.restart(), which re-runs preload on the SAME Phaser game; preloads queue() skips every texture where this.textures.exists(texture); so a relayout queues NOTHING, and Phaser fires no progress at all on an empty queue (LoaderPlugin.start calls loadComplete() directly for list.size === 0, phaser 3.90.0). A re-boot with nothing to load is exactly a load screen with no progress to show - which is what this frame draws: the load screen MINUS the bar and the caption. THAT IS A CANDIDATE, NOT A RULING, AND NOTHING WAS BUILT ON IT. The frame still carries no annotation of what raises it, and a relayout is not obviously what a designer means by refresh. DECISION FOR CASEY, as a choice: (a) this is the re-boot state - the boot screen drawn without bar or caption whenever the queue is empty, which the engine can detect today at no cost; (b) it is a browser page refresh or reconnect, which needs a session-restore state the engine does not have; (c) it is decoration with no trigger and the frame is ruled out. Separately and INDEPENDENT of the ruling, this pass fixed a real defect on the path (skai-gaming e601eb75): that same empty queue left this.progress on its initial 0, so every relayout held an EMPTY groove captioned Loading... 0% for the 320ms hold in create, under a comment promising a full bar. Whoever builds this frame draws the streak from the cosmic skins own STREAKS record (09e37a78 took engine-constant streaks off all five games). The boards six multiplier cells on 11146-1937 draw this bomb with their figure over it; what reads as a wrapper nub at thumbnail size is the fuse. It is NOT a reel symbol, which makes it the one of the three that could in principle be wired as cell art rather than as a paying symbol - and it is still not built, because a multiplier is a payout term and drawing one the engine neither implements nor pays is exactly what the fence forbids. VERIFIED AT HEAD THIS PASS, by source and not by memory, that wiring the ART alone cannot move the math: gem-slots/definition.ts:103 takes symbolKeys from the certified configs own paytable.symbols and :120 maps THOSE through gemSymbolArt, and every engine consumer reads definition.skin.symbols (BootScene.ts:166, ReelsScene.ts:298 and :590-595, PaytableScene.ts:120) - including the spin strips length. THE REAL BLOCKER IS THE ONE THE ART CANNOT ANSWER: what this symbol IS in the paytable. That is the certified configs to say and Caseys to rule, and gem_slots has no certified config at all today, so there is no paytable to add a key to. MONEY FENCE: nothing built, because building the art implies a symbol that pays. DECISION FOR CASEY, as a choice: (a) Sugar rush HAS a multiplier feature, and the certified config names its symbol and ceiling, at which point this art wires with it; (b) it has none and this master is ruled out; (c) hold. Note the boards also carry a free-spins caption claiming a multiplier ceiling, and skin.ts deliberately does not repeat that figure.
